reasoning: Roofline and NCU agree: compute SOL is 89.7% while memory SOL/DRAM throughput is 42.2%, so arithmetic throughput is the dominant limiter. Warp activity and issue utilization are both 100%, indicating the kernel is well-occupied and not stall-dominated; remaining headroom is mostly in compute efficiency rather than bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: High FP32/VALU math intensity from repeated dot-products and nonlinear activation in the inner loops saturates compute pipelines before memory.

evidence.interpretation: SM compute pipeline utilization is very high, close to peak sustained.

fixes.fix: Reduce FP32 work per output by using lower-precision math paths where acceptable (e.g., BF16/FP16 accumulation strategy or MFMA/Tensor-Core style reformulation) and fuse/simplify activation math.
fixes.rationale: Lower per-operation cost and higher math throughput directly target the saturated compute path.

root_causes.cause: Kernel structure performs multiple independent accumulator streams (acc0..acc7) and many reductions per TOPK/J/K tile, increasing instruction pressure and limiting additional throughput gains.

evidence.interpretation: Very large dynamic instruction count indicates heavy instruction-level compute workload.

fixes.fix: Retune tiling/unrolling (BLOCK_OUT, BLOCK_J, GROUP_N) to reduce redundant scalar/vector instructions and improve instruction efficiency per byte loaded.
fixes.rationale: Lowering instruction overhead for the same data movement improves compute-side headroom when ALUs are the bottleneck.
